objective:
Issue #18: the demo video (D-6, shipped in #6) does not play on iPhone. The <video> points straight at a GitHub Release asset, and GitHub serves it as "content-type: application/octet-stream" + "content-disposition: attachment"; iOS WebKit refuses to play a file declared that way (desktop Chrome sniffs and plays it). Fix: the dashboard server serves the video itself with the right headers.
1. src/server.ts: add GET /demo/:file where :file must match exactly /^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\.mp4$/ and the date must be in the snapshot directory listing (reuse snapshotDates(); never build a path or URL from raw input). Read that snapshot; take demo.videoUrl. Serve 404 (plain text) when the date is unknown, the snapshot has no demo or videoUrl is null, or videoUrl is not https:// on host github.com (prevents the server fetching arbitrary URLs).
2. Fetch videoUrl upstream with the global fetch (injectable for tests via a new optional AppOptions.fetch, default globalThis.fetch), redirect "follow", forwarding the request's Range header if present. Pass through the upstream status when it is 200, 206 or 416, and the headers Content-Length, Content-Range, Accept-Ranges (default "bytes" when absent), Last-Modified, ETag. Always set Content-Type: video/mp4 and Cache-Control: "private, max-age=300". Never send Content-Disposition. Stream the body (Readable.fromWeb), don't buffer it. Any other upstream status, a thrown fetch or a timeout (AbortSignal.timeout, 15 s for the response headers): 502 plain text "The demo video could not be loaded from GitHub." and log it.
3. The route sits behind the same basic auth as "/" (the existing onRequest hook already covers it; only /healthz is exempt; keep it that way) and HEAD must work.
4. src/page.ts demoCard: when httpUrl(d.videoUrl) is non-null, the <video src> becomes "/demo/<s.date>.mp4" instead of the GitHub URL; keep every other attribute. Add type="video/mp4" is NOT needed (src attribute stays). Nothing else on the page changes.

Every committed snapshot still renders.
